description.html: The terracotta-colored amphora gives an aquarium the look of an ancient shipwreck or a sunken city. It has two rounded handles, a wide neck decorated with engraved diamonds and a body with horizontal grooves. Symbols in the style of ancient Egypt are engraved on the belly, including a clearly visible ankh, so the piece looks like something found on a riverbed.

Fish can swim through the opening in the neck into the amphora and shelter inside. This kind of hide suits shy species and fish that like dark hiding places, because it gives them a place to rest and reduces stress. Depending on how you place it, the opening can face the glass or be hidden behind plants, so you decide how visible the fish are while they rest.

Before placing the amphora, rinse it with lukewarm water, without detergent or cleaning products. Set it directly on the bottom or bury it slightly in gravel or sand, so it stands steadily and fish cannot tip it over while digging. It can stand upright or lie on its side, as if it had fallen from a ship; turn the opening so it is visible from the front of the aquarium.
When algae builds up on the surface, take the amphora out and scrub it with a soft brush in clean water. It goes well with stones, roots and other ancient-style decorations from our equipment range.
